source: Q123 (2026-09-22): investigation of build_frames() bone-frame coverage and feasibility of adding a transverse axis to the 6 bones Q121 flagged (humerus, scapula, clavicle, mandible, hyoid, sternum). No transverse axis shipped this item -- see decisions below.
method: Re-ran build_frames() per subject, merged first-subject-wins in the EXACT subject order each real rebuild script uses (scripts/vhm_rebuild_bundle.sh, scripts/cryo/vhf_rebuild_bundle.sh), reproducing scripts/export_viewer_bundle.py's own resolve_anchor_points()/claim-order behavior directly rather than trusting a prior session's summary.

reconciliation_of_q121s_19_17_claim.q121_claim: build_frames() resolves 19 bones on the male (clavicle/femur/fibula/hip_bone/humerus/patella/radius/scapula/ulna, all r+l, plus hyoid/mandible/sternum) and 17 on the female (same set minus radius_l/ulna_l).

measured_true_state.discrepancy_found: Q121's claim that the female set is 'the same set minus radius_l/ulna_l' is WRONG. scapula_{l,r} resolves on the FEMALE but NOT on the male -- both counts happen to be 19, but the bone SETS differ (male has radius_l/ulna_l that the female lacks; female has scapula_l/r that the male lacks). Confirmed by two independent checks: (1) the frame merge above, (2) direct inspection of which real build subject carries each bone mesh.
measured_true_state.root_cause: scapula's own frame code (build_frames(), 'the upper body' section) requires the SAME subject's by_atlas_id to carry BOTH the scapula mesh AND an already-resolved humerus_{side} frame (the glenoid is located as the 2% of the scapula nearest the fitted humeral head centre). On the male, scapula ships in subject ct_vhm while humerus ships in a DIFFERENT subject (ct_vhm_arm) -- since build_frames() (and the real pipeline's resolve_anchor_points()) is called per-subject, scapula's frame never has a humerus frame available in the same call and so never resolves for the male, in the real, currently-published subject order. On the female, ct_vhf alone carries both scapula_{l,r} AND humerus_{l,r}, so it resolves. This is a data/subject-organization gap, not a code bug in build_frames() itself -- flagged here per this item's own instruction to verify precisely, not fixed (out of this item's scope, and fixing it would mean restructuring which subject a bone mesh ships from).

fitted_tag_by_bone.femur_l: long (BOTH bodies) -- the cartilage-based 'both' path (fit_sphere on femoral-head cartilage + epicondylar_axis on the distal condyles) NEVER triggers on any currently-shipped subject: this session's geometry carries fused cartilage names (knee_articular_cartilage_*, not *_femurhead/*_femurdistal), exactly the gap Q118 already found. Both bodies fall back to the CT-only path (long axis only, transverse explicitly left as convention). This reconciles the task's own background framing, which cites femur as the flagship full-transverse-frame example: that code path is real but is DEAD CODE on the currently shipped geometry for both subjects, not something this item changed.
fitted_tag_by_bone.tibia_l: NOT RESOLVED on either body -- no fallback path exists in build_frames() for tibia (unlike femur/hip_bone), so it never appears in frames at all on current geometry.
fitted_tag_by_bone.hip_bone_l: transverse (both bodies) -- the acetabular-sphere-or-femoral-head-substitute path DOES trigger even with fused cartilage naming, because it falls back per-side independently and its transverse axis (interacetabular line) only needs both femoral-head centres, which the CT fallback already provides.
fitted_tag_by_bone.radius_l: long (male only -- female's left forearm is documented elsewhere, Q39/Q41/Q43/Q71/Q97, as incomplete/absent)
fitted_tag_by_bone.tarsals_l/r, metatarsals_l/r, phalanges_: not resolved on either body in the real merged subject order (cartilage-filename dependency for tarsals; metatarsals/phalanges_foot need a tarsal_cloud AND rays present in the same subject, which the real foot subject does not co-carry with a resolvable tarsal frame currently)

humerus.candidate_method: epicondylar_axis()-style reuse: SVD widest-spread direction in the distal 6-22% of the raw humerus mesh (same code femur uses, no separate label needed).

measured.ct_vhm_arm_r: width 61.9-69.3 mm across frac 0.10-0.22, axis not bimodal

humerus.verdict: DECLINED. Left/right widths on the SAME specimen differ by 8-14 mm (male) and 12-14 mm/24% (female) -- anatomically implausible for a paired long bone (real biepicondylar asymmetry is normally 0-5 mm). Histogram of the projected distal band along the candidate axis shows NO bimodal separation on either body (no two-lobe/one-valley structure the way the femoral condyles show) -- the fit is not distinguishing two epicondyles at all, it is picking up the general anteroposterior flattening of the distal humerus (olecranon/coronoid fossae), which for this bone's shape rivals or exceeds its true mediolateral spread. The current shipped humerus mesh (TotalSegmentator whole-bone label for the CT-based subject, coarse ~2900-vertex STL-based mesh for the male) does not separately preserve the medial/lateral epicondyles as identifiable protrusions the way the femoral condyles are preserved. Cross-checked against bones.json's own hand-authored epicondyle local-X difference (40 mm) -- neither measured width (42-78mm) nor axis direction (Z-dominant, not X-dominant) is consistent with that authored assumption either. A real, geometry-derived transverse axis for the humerus is not achievable from this project's current label data without guessing which part of the spread is 'the epicondyles' -- exactly the class of decline this item's hard constraint calls for.

scapula.candidate_method: glenoid-to-acromion line as a fitted long axis (task's own suggestion: use the glenoid's own orientation / a paired asymmetric reference, not femur's method); coracoid process as a second point for a transverse.
scapula.measured: glenoid->acromion direction has world-Y component 0.945-0.956 on the female (both sides) -- close to, but not identical to, the existing world-Y convention already in use.
scapula.verdict: DECLINED FOR TIME/RIGOR, not for infeasibility (same class as Q118's gluteal_tendon_complex decline). The candidate long axis is real and close to world-aligned (lower structural risk than mandible's case below), but a genuinely validated SECOND, independent point (coracoid) was only sketched, not cross-body/quantile-stability validated the way mandible's intercondylar measurement or femur's sphere fit were, and scapula's frame already carries the largest blast radius of the 6 bones checked (12 anchors x2 sides + 22 landmarks) -- shipping an under-validated axis here risks exactly the invented-direction problem the hard constraint forbids. A good, scoped follow-up: validate the coracoid-based transverse the same way mandible's TMJ condyles were validated here (cross-body agreement, stability across a percentile sweep) before attempting the same before/after regression check.

clavicle.candidate_method: PCA (SVD) of the whole bone's own vertices, perpendicular to the already-fitted long axis (the S-curve's own bow direction) -- adds a transverse WITHOUT touching the already-working, already-authored-compatible long axis, unlike mandible/scapula/hyoid/sternum which start from 'neither'.
clavicle.measured_singular_value_ratio: 1.89-2.00 (both bodies, both sides) -- a real but only moderately dominant direction, well short of femur's or the TMJ condyles' much cleaner separation.
clavicle.before_after_regression_check: Directly re-placed clavicle's own existing 4 hand-authored landmarks (both bodies, both sides) through the candidate transverse-augmented frame and measured distance to the clavicle's own mesh surface, old vs new: MIXED result, not a clean improvement. 'conoid tubercle' and 'acromial end' improved by several mm on 3/4 sides (e.g. male_r conoid tubercle 5.2->0.9 mm), but 'deltoid tubercle / anterior border' WORSENED by 4-6 mm on 3/4 sides (e.g. male_l 2.1->7.5 mm, female_l 1.2->6.4 mm). No net, confident benefit across all 4 landmarks x2 sides x2 bodies.
clavicle.verdict: DECLINED. A real geometric signal exists (the curvature is measurable) but it does not reliably improve -- and materially worsens some -- of the clavicle's own already-authored, already-working landmarks. Shipping it would trade one landmark's accuracy for another's without a principled way to choose, which is not the kind of measured improvement this project's own standard requires.

mandible.candidate_method: TMJ condyles as two point clusters (superior 5% of the bone by height, split left/right of the midline) for a genuine long-axis (menton to condyle midpoint) + transverse (right-minus-left condyle) frame.

measured.intercondylar_width_male: 97.4-99.9 mm across percentile bands 0.85-0.97 of height
measured.cross_body_agreement: 99.5 mm (male) vs 100.4 mm (female), 0.9 mm apart -- the cleanest cross-body agreement found of any of the 6 bones, comparable to femur's own sphere-fit validation.
measured.bimodal_separation: a wide, genuinely empty gap (no vertices within ~30 mm of the midline in the superior 5% band, both bodies) -- the cleanest signal of the 6 bones, unlike humerus's smooth unimodal spread.

mandible.before_after_regression_check: Implemented the fitted long+transverse frame and re-ran scripts/audit_landmarks_vs_geometry.py directly on ct_vhm_head and ct_vhf_head. RESULT: median distance-to-bone-surface for the mandible's own 4 hand-authored landmarks went from 8.3 mm (male) / 4.2 mm (female) under the CURRENT convention to 25.4 mm (male) / 28.0 mm (female) under the fitted frame -- a large, unambiguous regression, not an improvement.
mandible.root_cause: The menton-to-condyle-midpoint direction is NOT close to world-vertical: the condyles sit well POSTERIOR to the menton (not just superior), so the fitted Y axis tilts 33-42 degrees off world Y (measured directly: Y=[0.02,0.84,-0.54] male, [0.05,0.75,-0.66] female). bones.json's existing mandible landmarks (condylar process, coronoid process, angle of mandible, digastric fossa) were authored assuming plain world-aligned axes (X=right, Y=up, Z=anterior) under the CURRENT origin-only convention, not a bone-intrinsic long axis. Re-placing those same numbers through the tilted fitted frame moves them far from their intended anatomical points.
mandible.verdict: DECLINED TO SHIP, despite finding the cleanest real geometric signal of all 6 bones. The TMJ condyles ARE a genuine, well-measured, cross-body-validated feature and a real full frame IS achievable here -- but only by re-authoring bones.json's mandible landmarks in the new frame's own coordinates, which is out of this item's scope (no already-authored landmark data was to be touched). Flagged clearly as the strongest candidate for a focused future item that budgets time to re-author the 4 mandible landmarks alongside the frame change, with the same before/after audit-script verification already run here.

hyoid.candidate_method: greater/lesser cornu as two lateral clusters, mirroring mandible's approach.
hyoid.measured: No bimodal separation at all: the mesh's own X range is asymmetric and off-centre (-17.8 to +34.2 mm on the male, not straddling world midline symmetrically) and a 16-bin histogram shows a smooth, roughly uniform distribution with no valley -- unlike mandible's dramatic empty gap.
hyoid.verdict: DECLINED. The greater/lesser cornu are not separately identifiable as distinct lobes in this project's current hyoid mesh (small, ~2000-2200 vertices, and asymmetric in a way that suggests either coarse segmentation or a genuinely fused/simplified horn shape at this resolution) -- there is no real, measurable two-cluster signal to fit an axis to, so no attempt was made to force one. Consistent with this item's own hard constraint against inventing a direction with no geometric support.

sternum.candidate_method: clavicular notches (paired SC-joint facets) as a left/right split in a superior band, mirroring mandible's approach; alternative of just adding a long axis (jugular notch to xiphoid tip) considered separately.
sternum.measured: Width from the naive X-sign split SHRINKS monotonically as the band narrows toward the true superior edge (39.7 mm at the 85th percentile down to 34.2 mm at the 93rd, male; 31.6 down to 26.2 mm, female) rather than stabilizing the way mandible's intercondylar width did -- evidence this is tracking the manubrium's continuously curving superior border, not two isolated notch facets.
sternum.verdict: DECLINED for the transverse axis: no stable, bimodal two-point signal exists in this mesh for the clavicular notches; a naive left/right split catches the general taper of the manubrium's edge, not two real facets, and forcing a threshold that 'looks stable' would be picking a number, not measuring a feature. A separate, still-real possible improvement -- fitting a LONG axis alone (jugular notch to xiphoid tip, both real, individually measurable extremes) -- was considered but NOT attempted this item: adding it would change sternum's 'fitted' tag from 'neither' to 'long', which activates Q43's along-axis length-scaling behaviour for any landmark on this bone, a distinct functional change needing its own before/after audit separate from the transverse-axis question this item was scoped to. Left as a scoped follow-up, not attempted here.

ligament_tendon_reattempt.checked: Cross-referenced data/derived/Q121_ligament_feasibility_audit.json's full declined-id list (50 bone_frame_blocked + 31 landmark_text_mismatch + 2 geometry_verification_failed) against the 6 bones investigated here.
ligament_tendon_reattempt.result: 0 newly resolvable. All 31 landmark_text_mismatch declines are blocked by landmark TEXT not matching bones.json (a naming problem, unrelated to any bone's transverse-axis coverage -- unaffected by anything a transverse axis could fix). The 2 geometry_verification_failed declines (transverse_humeral_ligament_{r,l}) are the ONE case genuinely blocked by humerus's missing transverse axis, exactly as Q121 and this item's own background describe -- and remain declined, since the humerus investigation above concluded no reliable transverse axis is achievable from this project's current label data. No Q118 tendon declines were re-examined for a similar transverse-specific dependency beyond what Q121 already covers, since none of the 6 bones gained a working transverse axis this item.
